trace: E2 — the worked example of 4.6, end to end
note: The chain the contract claims composes: a trigger names a TASK, the task's read-order names OPERATIONS, the operations are served by the SURFACE. Nothing here is new machinery — that is the point of the example. `lifecycle` and `document` are two of the eight operations, called exactly as any other consumer calls them. A binding is a caller, not a new kind of surface.
read_order: 2. document   → migration-guide.json, where support.status is deprecated
3. (C) the consumer's own SSRF guard on any URL it resolves — never the surface's

findings.summary: declared replacement is in a different purl namespace

assertions.level_is_must_because: MIRI-CONSUMER-032 — a namespace-divergent replacement is the replacement-redirect attack (Lifecycle and Security Metadata 9.3). The level comes from the Consumer Conformance profile, never from the served document.
assertions.quote_is_attributed: `quote` holds publisher bytes and must be rendered as attributed data, never adopted as the consumer's own assertion (MIRI-CONSUMER-020, MIRI-CONSUMER-022).
assertions.namespace_comparison: PyPI has no namespace, so the comparison is on PEP 503 normalized distribution names — `greet-adversarial` vs `attacker-successor`. A substring test is not sufficient and was the original defect in MIRI-CONSUMER-032.
assertions.must_not: Auto-migrate onto the declared replacement. MIRI-CONSUMER-032 requires human confirmation; a consumer that rewrites call sites here performs the supply-chain attack itself.

why_this_case: It is the trace every other one is measured against: the only one where the full read-order is exercised and a must-level finding is the correct answer.
